newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says Britain best placed to compete in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says Britain best placed to compete in EMU.

text.p: Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday that Britain was "best placed of any European country to compete within a single currency."

In an bylined article in the Sun newspaper, Chancellor of the Exchequer Clarke dismissed the notion that "Britain won't be able to hack it in a single currency, that we need to hang on to the option of devaluing our way out of a crisis. That we won't be able to keep our borrowing and debts down."

The Sun article was a stout restatement of the government's "wait-and-see" approach to joining a single currency, which Clarke was forced to defend at the start of an often angry debate in the House of Commons on Wednesday.

In the article, Clarke said European Monetary Union (EMU) "could make us better off. It could be good news for business. Set up right, it could cut interest rates. Any policy offering those possibilities must be worth a second look."
Clarke said Britain would continue to push for strict rules for EMU, saying the "worst threat to British prosperity would come if Europe went ahead with EMU and it fell apart."
That meant "keeping out countries who cheat. Keeping out those who can only make it under the wire one year but can't stand the demands long term," Clarke said.
He added that Britain should "keep the right to say no if the others fudge it and make a mess of the plans, or if for any other reason we just don't fancy it."
